```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

```{r load-packages}
library(tidyverse)
library(randomForest)
library(recipes)
library(themis)
library(pROC)

options(bdat602.source_only = TRUE)
source("courses/bdat-602/_teacher/resources/datasets/simulate_bdat602_data.R")
health_data <- simulate_bdat602(n = 50000, seed = 602)
```

```{r split-data}
set.seed(602)
idx   <- sample(nrow(health_data), 0.80 * nrow(health_data))
train <- health_data[idx, ]
test  <- health_data[-idx, ]
```

## Task 1: Document class imbalance and the accuracy paradox

```{r task1-imbalance}
cat("Churn rate (train):", round(mean(train$churned), 3), "\n")
cat("Churn rate (test): ", round(mean(test$churned),  3), "\n")
```

```{r task1-naive}
naive_preds <- rep(0, nrow(test))
naive_acc   <- mean(naive_preds == test$churned)
cat("Naive 'always No' accuracy:", round(naive_acc, 3), "\n")
cat("Recall of naive model:      0 (catches zero churners)\n")
# ~82% accuracy but 0% recall — the accuracy paradox in action.
```

## Task 2: Class-weighted random forest

```{r task2-rf-weighted}
set.seed(602)
rf_wt <- randomForest(
  factor(churned) ~ age + plan_tier + income + num_claims + support_calls +
                    auto_pay + customer_rating + deductible,
  data       = train,
  ntree      = 200,
  classwt    = c("0" = 1, "1" = 5),
  importance = TRUE
)
print(rf_wt)
```

```{r task2-compare-recall}
prob_wt   <- predict(rf_wt, test, type = "prob")[, "1"]
pred_wt   <- factor(ifelse(prob_wt > 0.5, 1, 0), levels = c(0, 1))
cm_wt     <- table(Predicted = pred_wt, Actual = factor(test$churned))
recall_wt <- cm_wt["1", "1"] / sum(cm_wt[, "1"])

cat("Weighted RF recall at 0.5 threshold:", round(recall_wt, 3), "\n")
# Significantly higher than the naive 0 — class weights help the model
# identify churners even though they are a minority.
```

## Task 3: SMOTE oversampling

```{r task3-smote-recipe}
train_fac <- train |>
  mutate(churned = factor(churned, levels = c(0, 1)))

rec_smote <- recipe(
  churned ~ age + plan_tier + income + num_claims + support_calls +
            auto_pay + customer_rating + deductible,
  data = train_fac
) |>
  step_impute_median(all_numeric_predictors()) |>
  step_impute_mode(all_nominal_predictors()) |>
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors()) |>
  step_smote(churned, over_ratio = 1) |>
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors())

train_smote <- rec_smote |> prep(training = train_fac) |> bake(new_data = NULL)
```

```{r task3-check-balance}
cat("Class distribution after SMOTE:\n")
print(table(train_smote$churned))
# Both classes should now have approximately equal counts.
```

## Task 4: Compare models with precision-recall

```{r task4-rf-smote}
set.seed(602)
rf_smote <- randomForest(
  churned ~ .,
  data  = train_smote,
  ntree = 200
)

test_fac   <- test |> mutate(churned = factor(churned, levels = c(0, 1)))
prob_smote <- predict(rf_smote, test_fac, type = "prob")[, "1"]
```

```{r task4-f1-threshold}
f1_at <- function(prob, truth, threshold) {
  pred <- factor(ifelse(prob > threshold, 1, 0), levels = c(0, 1))
  cm   <- table(pred, truth)
  TP   <- cm["1", "1"]; FP <- cm["1", "0"]; FN <- cm["0", "1"]
  P    <- if ((TP + FP) == 0) 0 else TP / (TP + FP)
  R    <- if ((TP + FN) == 0) 0 else TP / (TP + FN)
  if ((P + R) == 0) 0 else 2 * P * R / (P + R)
}

cat("Weighted RF F1 at 0.3:", round(f1_at(prob_wt,    factor(test$churned), 0.3), 3), "\n")
cat("Weighted RF F1 at 0.5:", round(f1_at(prob_wt,    factor(test$churned), 0.5), 3), "\n")
cat("SMOTE RF   F1 at 0.3:", round(f1_at(prob_smote, factor(test$churned), 0.3), 3), "\n")
cat("SMOTE RF   F1 at 0.5:", round(f1_at(prob_smote, factor(test$churned), 0.5), 3), "\n")
```

```{r task4-pr-curve}
thresholds <- seq(0.05, 0.95, by = 0.05)

pr_both <- bind_rows(
  map_dfr(thresholds, function(thr) {
    pred <- factor(ifelse(prob_wt > thr, 1, 0), levels = c(0, 1))
    cm <- table(pred, factor(test$churned))
    TP <- cm["1","1"]; FP <- cm["1","0"]; FN <- cm["0","1"]
    P  <- if ((TP+FP)==0) 0 else TP/(TP+FP)
    R  <- if ((TP+FN)==0) 0 else TP/(TP+FN)
    tibble(threshold = thr, precision = P, recall = R, model = "Weighted RF")
  }),
  map_dfr(thresholds, function(thr) {
    pred <- factor(ifelse(prob_smote > thr, 1, 0), levels = c(0, 1))
    cm <- table(pred, factor(test$churned))
    TP <- cm["1","1"]; FP <- cm["1","0"]; FN <- cm["0","1"]
    P  <- if ((TP+FP)==0) 0 else TP/(TP+FP)
    R  <- if ((TP+FN)==0) 0 else TP/(TP+FN)
    tibble(threshold = thr, precision = P, recall = R, model = "SMOTE RF")
  })
)

ggplot(pr_both, aes(x = recall, y = precision, colour = model)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(title = "Precision-Recall Curves: Weighted RF vs. SMOTE RF",
       x = "Recall", y = "Precision") +
  theme_minimal()

# Both models outperform the naive baseline (which achieves recall = 0).
# SMOTE typically achieves slightly higher PR-AUC because it adds genuine
# diversity to the minority class rather than just reweighting the loss.
# The best threshold for F1 is typically around 0.25-0.40 for imbalanced churn data.
```

## Task 5: Class-weighted Spark random forest

```{r task5-spark-setup, eval=FALSE}
library(sparklyr)
library(dplyr)

sc <- spark_connect(master = "local[*]", version = "3.4.1")

options(bdat602.source_only = TRUE)
source("courses/bdat-602/_teacher/resources/datasets/simulate_bdat602_data.R")
health_full <- simulate_bdat602(n = 500000, seed = 602)
health_tbl  <- copy_to(sc, health_full, name = "health_ins", overwrite = TRUE)
```

```{r task5-spark-weights, eval=FALSE}
churn_rate      <- health_tbl |>
  summarise(rate = mean(churned, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  collect() |> pull(rate)

minority_weight <- (1 - churn_rate) / churn_rate
cat("Churn rate:", round(churn_rate, 3),
    "| Minority weight:", round(minority_weight, 2), "\n")
# Churn ~0.18 → weight ≈ 4.6 — each minority record counts as ~4.6 majority records

health_tbl <- health_tbl |>
  mutate(
    sample_weight = ifelse(churned == 1, minority_weight, 1.0),
    plan_tier_num = case_when(
      plan_tier == "Bronze"   ~ 1L, plan_tier == "Silver"   ~ 2L,
      plan_tier == "Gold"     ~ 3L, plan_tier == "Platinum" ~ 4L
    )
  )
```

```{r task5-spark-train, eval=FALSE}
splits      <- sdf_random_split(health_tbl,
                                training = 0.80, test = 0.20, seed = 602)
train_spark <- splits$training
test_spark  <- splits$test

spark_rf_wt <- train_spark |>
  ml_random_forest_classifier(
    formula    = churned ~ age + plan_tier_num + income + num_claims +
                           support_calls + auto_pay + customer_rating,
    num_trees  = 100,
    weight_col = "sample_weight",
    seed       = 602
  )
```

```{r task5-spark-eval, eval=FALSE}
preds_spark <- ml_predict(spark_rf_wt, test_spark)

auc_spark <- ml_binary_classification_evaluator(
  preds_spark,
  label_col          = "churned",
  raw_prediction_col = "rawPrediction",
  metric_name        = "areaUnderROC"
)
cat("Weighted Spark RF ROC-AUC:", round(auc_spark, 3), "\n")

# The Spark AUC is typically similar to or slightly higher than the local weighted RF.
# With 400,000 training rows (vs. 40,000 locally), the model sees more real minority
# examples, which partly compensates for not using SMOTE. The key advantage of Spark
# here is not dramatically better AUC but the ability to train on the full portfolio
# without memory constraints — critical for production insurance scoring.

spark_disconnect(sc)
```
